header: The fonts of the PDF, registered once. They are embedded in the file (so it looks the same everywhere), and I load them from /fonts/pdf/ only when a PDF is made. Source Sans 3 body text (regular, semibold, bold, italic) Poppins headings (semibold, bold: the same face as the app) Source Sans 3 (latin-ext) the rupee sign, which the latin file lacks Noto Sans Devanagari / Baloo Da 2 Hindi / Bengali text inside a reply WHY I use Baloo Da 2 for Bengali: the PDF library's text shaper mis-draws Bengali conjuncts and vowel signs (স্ক, স্থ, ব্যবস্থা, ছুটি) with Noto Sans Bengali, while Chrome draws the same font right; Baloo Da 2 (a sans face) is drawn right by the library, checked word by word against Chrome on all 90 Bengali words of the archive. All are open-licence fonts (SIL OFL; the licence texts are in /public/fonts/pdf/). The formats are WOFF because the PDF library reads TTF and WOFF, not WOFF2.
